note: Informational record of the bug CATEGORIES the hidden oracle (oracle_test.ts, written transiently by grader.py) checks for. The builder writes localCalendarDayKey()/isSameLocalDay() from scratch -- nothing is literally injected into its code. 'Seeded' here means 'plausible implementation mistakes a cheap builder model might make against this exact spec', which is what the oracle is designed to catch independent of whatever the spec-writer's own acceptance tests happened to cover.

bugs.description: Builds the day key from date.getUTCFullYear()/getUTCMonth()/getUTCDate() (or date.toISOString().slice(0,10)), ignoring the timeZone parameter entirely -- always returns the UTC calendar day regardless of what timezone was requested.

Builds the day key from date.getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate() (the host machine's own local timezone) instead of the requested timeZone parameter -- a different wrong code path than the UTC-components bug, though it happens to produce the same wrong answer in a UTC-TZ CI environment.

Resolves timeZone to a fixed numeric UTC-offset lookup table (e.g. 'America/New_York' -> always -5) instead of using proper IANA tzdata-aware resolution (Intl.DateTimeFormat or equivalent) -- gives the wrong calendar day for any date that falls in the OTHER half of the year's DST schedule from whatever the lookup table assumed.

Computes local time as date.getTime() - offsetMs instead of + offsetMs (or vice versa) when manually applying a UTC-offset lookup -- flips every non-UTC timezone's result by double the offset, breaking even DST-free zones like Asia/Tokyo or Pacific/Honolulu.

Returns the day key in a different field order or separator than YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. MM-DD-YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, or an unpadded '2026-7-15') -- isSameLocalDay's boolean comparisons can still happen to pass by accident (same wrong format on both sides), but localCalendarDayKey's own direct return value violates the spec'd format.

isSameLocalDay() is wired to call localCalendarDayKey(a, 'UTC') / localCalendarDayKey(b, 'UTC') (or omits the parameter) instead of passing through its own timeZone argument -- a composition/wiring bug distinct from localCalendarDayKey's own correctness, since localCalendarDayKey itself may be correctly implemented and still get called wrong.
